catalog_quote: In Motuna, every vowel or consonant in rhyme position constitutues one mora. That is, every vowel or C2 consonant constitutes one mora. ... First, stress generally falls on the third mora from the last in the case of words consisting of three or more moras, and on the first mora in the case of words consisting of two moras, if such a mora is a vowel or an archinasal. If such a mora happens to be /Q/ or /H/, stress falls on the preceding vowel. cf. §2.5. ... 2.5 STRESS. Stress is predictable, and thus is not phonemic in Motuna. (1) Most words consisting of three or more moras are pronounced with a relatively level high pitch from the beginning till the third mora from the last, which is immediately followed by another mora showing significantly steep drop in pitch. ... audit.reasoning: The classification (predictable stress on the third mora from the end, first mora in bimoraic words; moras = vowels and coda /H Q N/; retraction off voiceless /H Q/; word domain; listed exceptions) rests on the standard and only reference grammar of Motuna (Onishi 1994 ANU thesis, 565 pp.), whose stress section is backed by the author's own F0 measurements. We hold the full open-access text and every part of the deciding quotation, the domain quotation and the exceptions footnote is present verbatim at the stated sections/pages. Glottolog 5.1 lists no better or later independent description: the 2011 LINCOM grammar is the thesis republished (OGFAUS 09), and Gasaway 1987 is a short unpublished SIL ms that Onishi cites and supersedes. Nothing downloaded contradicts the record; no reclassification or re-read is indicated. Files touched: held source above; listing pages
